title: Distinct Pairs
description:
You are given an array A of length N.

You have two functions defined as follows:
• frequency(left, right, value): Returns the number of elements in the range [left, right] that are equal to value.
• distinct(left, right): Returns the number of distinct elements in the range [left, right].

Find the number of pairs (i, j) that satisfy the following condition:
frequency(1, i, A[i]) + frequency(j, N, A[j]) <= [distinct(1, i) / 2] + [distinct(j, N) / 2].

Since the answer can be very large, return it modulo 10^9+7.

Note:
• Here [X] represents the greatest integer less than or equal to X.
• 1 <= i < j <= N
• The array uses 1-based indexing for the range function parameters.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer, N, denoting the number of elements in A.
Each line i of the N subsequent lines (where 0 <= i < N) contains an integer describing A[i].
outputFormat: Print a single integer denoting the number of valid pairs (i, j) modulo 10^9+7.

examples.explanation:
Given N=5, A=[2, 2, 3, 1, 5].
We can select two pairs (1, 2) and (3, 4) which satisfy the given conditions.
Hence, the answer for this case is equal to 2.

Given N=5, A=[2, 2, 3, 1, 5] (Wait, PDF explanation has a typo copying array from Case 1. The input is actually [5, 5, 5, 5, 5]).
There exists no pair which satisfy the given conditions.
Hence, the answer for this case is equal to 0.

Given N=5, A=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5].
There are 5 pairs which satisfy the following conditions are (1, 2), (2, 3), (2, 4), (3, 4), (4, 5) (Note: PDF explanation explicitly mentions 5 valid pairs).
Hence, the answer for this case is equal to 5.
